Select elements from objects with class "canregs", or "fbswicds"

Source: R/cr_select.R
cr_select.Rd

This function allows you to select specific elements from objects of class 'canregs', 'fbswicds', or 'asrs' based on provided indices, logical conditions, or expressions. The selected elements are returned while preserving the class of the input object.

Usage

cr_select(data, ..., index = names(data))

# S3 method for class 'canregs'
cr_select(data, ..., index = names(data))

# S3 method for class 'asrs'
cr_select(data, ..., index = names(data))

# S3 method for class 'age_rates'
cr_select(data, ..., index = names(data))

# S3 method for class 'fbswicds'
cr_select(data, ..., index = names(data))

# S3 method for class 'summaries'
cr_select(data, ..., index = names(data))

Arguments

data

An object of class 'canregs', 'fbswicds', or 'asrs' from which elements will be selected.

...

Optional conditions or expressions used to filter elements within the list or data frame. Conditions are evaluated for each element of the input object. For canregs and fbswicds, population-year expressions can refer to POP or pop, respectively. The aliases pop_years, pop_n_years, pop_year_min, pop_year_max, and pop_year_range are also available. They mean: pop_years is the sorted unique non-missing population year labels; pop_n_years is the number of those years; pop_year_min and pop_year_max are the minimum and maximum calendar-year bounds; and pop_year_range is a length-two vector containing those bounds. Period labels such as "2003-2007" contribute 2003 and 2007 to the respective bounds. For example, use all(pop_years %in% as.character(2018:2022)) to require all population years to fall within 2018–2022.

index

A vector of indices specifying the elements to select. This can be a character vector (matching element names), a numeric vector (specifying positions), or a logical vector (indicating inclusion).

Value

An object of the same class as the input object, containing only the selected elements that meet the specified indices or conditions.

Details

Each comma-separated condition must be satisfied by at least one non-missing value within an element. The conditions may be satisfied by different rows. To require conditions on the same row, combine them with & in a single expression. Missing condition values do not count as matches.

Examples

data("canregs")
# Select elements which mi greather than 0.5 from `canregs`
canregs_mi <- cr_select(canregs, mi > 0.5)
# Select registries with population data for exactly three years
canregs_three_years <- cr_select(canregs, pop_n_years == 3)
# Select registries whose population years are all within 2018--2022
canregs_period <- cr_select(
  canregs,
  all(pop_years %in% as.character(2018:2022))
)
# The original population data can also be used directly
canregs_three_years <- cr_select(
  canregs,
  length(unique(POP$year)) == 3
)

# Select elements from obejct with class of `fbswicds`
fbsws <- count_canreg(canregs)
# Select elements which `inci` greater than 250 per 100000 population
fbsws_inci <- cr_select(fbsws, inci > 250)

# Select elements from object with class of `summaries`
summ <- summary(canregs, collapse = FALSE)
# Select elements for whcih `mi` greater than 0.5
summ_mi <- cr_select(summ, mi > 0.5)
names(summ_mi)
#> [1] "411721"
